title: Makonde Cassava Bread
community: Makonde people of Mtwara — cassava flour bread of the southern plateau
author: Mama Salima
desc: Makonde Cassava Bread — cassava flour mixed with water and a little coconut milk, formed into flat rounds and pan-fried in the Makonde tradition. Naturally gluten-free, slightly chewy, and deeply satisfying — the daily bread of southern Tanzania's cassava country.
longDesc: Makonde cassava bread is the staple bread of Mtwara — where cassava is the dominant crop, cassava flour is also the primary flour. This simple pan-fried bread is made daily from the same cassava that goes into the stew, reflecting the Makonde's complete dependency on and mastery of this single crop.
steps: Mix cassava flour, coconut milk, and salt.
Add warm water gradually, mixing until a soft but not sticky dough forms.
Divide into 8 balls. Flatten each into a round 1cm thick.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat.
Cook each round 4—5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
chefTips: Cassava dough is naturally gluten-free — do not expect it to behave like wheat dough.
It will not puff up like chapati — it stays flat and dense.
commonMistakes: Expecting it to rise or puff — it will not.
cookingScience: Cassava flour contains no gluten — when formed into dough, the binding comes from cassava starch gelatinisation (heated cassava starch absorbs water and becomes tacky). The coconut milk fat helps produce a more tender, less brittle result.
sustainabilityTips: Cassava is the most drought-tolerant staple — perfect for Mtwara's challenging climate.
culturalNote: Makonde cassava bread is the daily bread of southern Tanzania — made every morning from the cassava flour ground the day before, eaten with the cassava stew, lived entirely within the world of one remarkable crop.
